warnings: Shader (highest impact): drive fire color from temperature via blackbody explicitly. In the domain material, use Temperature -> Map Range to a hotter range (e.g. 1200–3800K, not capped around ~2200K) and feed that into a Blackbody node; plug Blackbody color into Principled Volume Emission Color. Keep Blackbody Intensity at 1.0 and use Flame to drive Emission Strength (with a stronger multiplier).

Boost emission contrast: increase the Flame→Emission Strength multiplier significantly (e.g. 35 → 100–250) and reduce volume Density so it doesn’t turn into a thick white fog. Aim for a bright core with lower surrounding density.

Rebalance density sources: reduce or remove the smoke Density contribution for a “fire-only” look (or heavily downscale it). Use Flame (or Heat) more than Density for the visible volume when you want a clean flame plume.
Simulation detail: increase domain resolution (64 is typically too low for a close, small indoor flame). Try 128 as a minimum; 192–256 for close-up production shots. Then rebake.

Turbulence: increase vorticity and flame vorticity, and ensure noise/high-res detail is enabled and strong enough to break the laminar column look (increase noise strength and adjust noise scale for finer detail).
Rendering quality: lower Cycles Volume Step Size / increase volumetric sampling to reduce banding/stepping (at the cost of render time). Increase samples if needed after fixing emission.

Emitter/base: slightly enlarge the flow emitter volume and/or soften the base falloff so the flame doesn’t appear abruptly clipped at the bottom; verify the domain fully contains the visible plume with margin.
Lighting integration: once emission is correct, verify the volume is actually contributing light (Cycles) and consider modest bloom/glare only for the hottest core (avoid blooming the whole column).
